newsitem.title: FRANCE: No stability pact deal at Amsterdam -Moscovici.
newsitem.headline: No stability pact deal at Amsterdam -Moscovici.

text.p: French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici said on Monday that a stability pact to limit the budget deficits of countries that join a single European currency could not be approved at next week's Amsterdam EU summit.

Interviewed by France-Info radio, he said France's new government needed more time to evaluate the content of the pact, negotiated by its centre-right predecessors, and to press for additional clauses.

"We do not reject the stability pact but we are saying that the regulations which are meant to put it into effect cannot be accepted as they stand today," Moscovici said, echoing comments by Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn to EU colleagues in Luxembourg earlier on Monday.
"We have asked for a delay. We want to make an evaluation. But we think that to make this evaluation will take more than one week and thus it cannot be concluded in Amsterdam," the minister said.
The June 16-17 Amsterdam summit had been due to formally approve the pact, to be signed by ministers afterwards.

Moscovici said France wanted to add two clauses, one enshrining the coordination of economic policies among EU member states by what he called an "economic government" and the other setting out a European growth initiative to promote employment.

While it was clear that the philosophy of the stability pact agreed last December in Dublin did not reflect the Socialist party's wishes, France had given its word in the negotiations and would not go back on it now.
Moscovici insisted the new government was utterly committed to launching the single currency on time in 1999 and meeting the Maastricht treaty conditions for monetary union.
